- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes; true values often dip within 5–7 days.
- Underestimate downward corrections after strong upward moves; sentiment spikes (positive sentiment) often trigger overconfidence in continuation.
- When sentiment is negative (especially > -1.5), reduce forecasted price by 5–10% relative to model output.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion is strong in the 10–15 day horizon; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 10–20%.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5 days of the 30-day window; apply a 3–5 day lag correction for early values.
